newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian activists sentenced for subversion.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian activists sentenced for subversion.

text.p: An Indonesian court on Tuesday sentenced two left-wing activists accused of fomenting labour strife to four and six years in jail for subversion.

The court in Indonesia's second largest city of Surabaya sentenced Dita Indah Sari, 30, to six years in jail and Coen Husein Pontoh, 27, to four years for manipulating, undermining and deviating from state policy guidelines.
"The defendants have been found guilty of subversion," presiding judge Amrin Boer said in his ruling.
The two, who were accused of organising a major strike in Surabaya last July involving up to 20,000 workers, said they would appeal against the verdict. Subversion carries a maximum penalty of death.

Sari and Pontoh are members of the unrecognised left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD). Sari heads the PRD's labour wing, the Indonesian Workers Struggle Centre, while Pontoh is an official of the affiliated Indonesian Farmers Union.
"This verdict is unfair. I will continue my struggle for the workers," Sari said after the judgment was pronounced in a courtroom packed with about 100 supporters.
About 200 soldiers and policemen were stationed outside the court building.
Government prosecutors had asked the court to sentence Sari and Pontoh to eight years and six years respectively.
The same court will hand down a verdict on Wednesday on another PRD member, Mohammad Soleh, who faces a five-year jail term for subversion in relation to the strike.

Five other members of the PRD, including its leader Budiman Sudjatmiko, face jail sentences of eight to 15 years for spreading hatred against the government in relation to riots in Jakarta last July which the authorities blamed on the group.

The riots erupted after police and a government-backed faction of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) raided the PDI headquarters and evicted supporters of ousted party chief Megawati Sukarnoputri.
At least five people were killed in the riots, the worst violence in Jakarta for more than two decades.
